subject: Clarification on multi-year prepay true-up mechanics and exceptions
messages:
From: Alice Johnson <alice@cloudlytics.com>

Cc: Bob Reeves <bob.reeves@cloudlytics.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification on multi-year prepay true-up mechanics and exceptions

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the demo last week — CloudLytics is interested in a 3-year prepay but we need to make sure the true-up/overage language and the ramp schedule won't create unexpected billing or operational complexity for our finance team. A few specific asks: 

- Can you confirm how Redwood calculates end-of-term true-ups versus annual true-ups? Is it strictly annual reconciliations or do you also support final true-up at contract expiry with different treatment?
- We typically ramp in the first year (50%->75%->100% year-over-year). Will Redwood allow a smoothing approach so we aren't billed for large front-loaded commits?
- What are acceptable "exceptions" to true-up (e.g., M&A, data migration delays, force majeure)? Do those get buffer-band treatment or formal credits?
- Would you provide a worked example (amortization) for a 3-year, $1.2M prepay with the ramp above and a 10% buffer band?

If you can send a short one-pager and a sample spreadsheet demonstrating the math, we can take it to procurement next week.

Appreciate it — cc'ing Bob (finance) to keep him in the loop.

Best,
Alice Johnson
Head of Cloud Strategy
CloudLytics

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com

Cc: Bob Reeves <bob.reeves@cloudlytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 31 May 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification on multi-year prepay true-up mechanics and exceptions

Alice — thanks for the clear list. Below are answers at a high level and attached is a draft term sheet plus a worked spreadsheet that models several ramp/true-up permutations.

Summary answers:
- True-up cadence: we support both annual true-ups (typical) and a final end-of-term true-up at expiry. For multi-year agreements we normally do annual reconciliations and then an end-of-term settlement that accounts for any carryforward or credits from earlier years.
- Smoothing/ramp: we offer a ramp smoothing option where committed units are annualized across months for billing consistency; operationally we allocate capacity to meet the annualized profile and maintain a 60–90 day buffer band (configurable) before overage charges kick in.
- Exceptions: standard carve-outs (M&A, paid migration extension, regulatory hold) can be handled via negotiated credits or temporary suspension; these are treated separately from buffer-band calculations and require written approval.
- Worked example: see trueup-examples.xlsx for a 3-year $1.2M case with 50/75/100 ramp and a 10% buffer band. The spreadsheet shows monthly amortization, carryforward caps, and how credits apply on final settlement.

Key commercial bullets from the draft term sheet (attached):
- Yearly committed USD and effective unit price locked for term; multi-year discount tiers shown (year 1 = 12%, year 2 = 14%, year 3 = 16% elected discount band is hypothetical in sheet)
- Carryforward allowed up to 25% of a year's committed volume, but credits cannot exceed 12% of committed spend per year
- Buffer band default 90 days; customer may request 60 days for promotional/aggressive ramps
- Final true-up: credits applied first against outstanding consumption, remaining overage billed at agreed overage rate; refunds are rare and only handled at executive discretion

Next steps: Marissa (cc) will help with legal redline route; Vanessa can work procurement cadence. If you want, we can hop on a 30-min call Wednesday to walk through the spreadsheet.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher

Subject: Re: Clarification on multi-year prepay true-up mechanics and exceptions

Couple of internal clarifications / asks before we take this to legal: 

- Carryforward cap: propose we make the carryforward cap 25% but cap monetary credit at 10% of that year's committed spend (keeps exposure bounded).
- Buffer band exceptions: anything claiming M&A or force majeure must include evidence and an agreed remediation window; otherwise treat as normal buffer-band flow.
- Discount floors: any multi-year tier that implies >22% effective discount needs VP approval.
- Amortization rounding: in the spreadsheet, round overages to the nearest month and bill monthly to align with invoicing practices.

I'll attach a marked-up redline for legal. Also suggest we add a short clause that allows one-time migration credit (up to $X) if we jointly agree on a migration plan within the first 120 days.

Marissa Cole
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
